_note: Full RFC 9421 proof-of-possession SIGNING vectors for the bound-retrieval GET (ADR-013 D1/D3). Copied verbatim from the protocol SDK's own generated corpus at sdk/go/helpers/testdata/pop-vectors.json in module github.com/RAMP-Protocol/protocol, whose generator is the emitter and drift gate. The SDK is the source of truth: refresh this copy from there rather than editing values by hand. Copied rather than read from the module cache because testdata cannot cross a module boundary (go:embed will not reach it) and a cache read breaks in vendored or air-gapped CI; testdata/thumbprint-vectors.json is the same arrangement. internal/httpsig/pop_test.go reads this file: it signs through the module and compares all three emitted headers, so a drift between the copy and the pinned module fails the build here rather than at an edge. Where pop-signature-base-vectors.json pins only the signature BASE string, these pin the emitted wire values end to end: presented_key_b64url is the X-RAMP-Agent-Key value (base64url-no-pad raw 32-byte public key), signature_input and signature are the header values verbatim, and signature is STANDARD base64 inside the byte-string colons while the key is base64url — an encoding asymmetry that a hand-written signer gets wrong silently. signer_seed_hex is the RFC 8032 seed the private key is derived from. The wrong_key vector signs with a different key than agent_id names, so on the VERIFIER side its signature is an independent byte pin; on the signer side the SDK refuses to mint it at all, and the Go reader pins that refusal instead. expected_valid and now_unix describe verifier outcomes and are unused by a signer-side test.
